info.name: QuickJoiner API — connected flow
info.description:
An end-to-end runbook for driving QuickJoiner over its HTTP API: check health, (optionally) sign in, connect a source, sync it, watch progress, then query the learned memory and graph. Requests are chained — test scripts capture the bearer token, connector name, and a session id into collection variables, so you can run the whole folder top-to-bottom with the Collection Runner.

Set the `baseUrl` variable (default http://localhost:8787). Auth is OPTIONAL: skip the Authentication folder to run in open mode; run it once to turn auth on and capture a token for the rest.

Streaming note: /api/chat, /api/scrape and /api/sync/{name}/logs return Server-Sent Events (text/event-stream). Postman shows the raw stream; read `data:` lines until a `done` event.

variable.value: How do we deploy and roll back?

variable.description: A web_scrape connector with use_browser=true (a site behind a login)
A .zip containing SKILL.md, for the install request
The skill to configure or remove
One environment-variable name a skill requires (your credential)
A doc_id from one of YOUR OWN private documents (GET /api/sources/notes:<you>/documents, or `qj promotions mine`).

exec: console.log('org:', s.org, '| model:', s.llm.model, '| docs:', s.stats.documents);

item.name: 1 · Authentication (optional)
item.description: Run ONCE to turn auth on + capture a token. Skip entirely to stay in open mode.

request.description: Every user + RBAC role (admin | editor | viewer). Admin only.

Set {{targetUser}}'s role to admin | editor | viewer. Admin only. Roles gate the whole API: viewers read/ask, editors also connect/sync/teach, admins additionally manage settings, reset memory, and administer users.

item.name: List connector types
item.description: The catalog of connector types and each type's configurable fields (required / secret flags) plus supported `modes`. Use it to fill `options` on the next request. A type may also carry `next_step` — what to do AFTER saving, for connectors that aren't usable the moment they're created (OneDrive needs an interactive Microsoft 365 sign-in, which can only happen once the connector exists). Each field carries `multiline` — true for prose fields a UI should render as a textarea. Every type has one: `extraction_prompt`, an optional description of what this source's documents contain, which guides knowledge-graph extraction for it (needs `graph.extract_triples` on in /api/settings).

item.name: Create a 'files' connector
item.description: Point `connectorPath` at a real folder first. Swap type/options for git/github/jira/etc. — see the connector types response for each type's fields.

item.name: Rename connector (before first sync)
item.description: Rename — allowed ONLY before the first sync (0 documents), since the name keys every document/vector/graph node/watermark it would ingest. 409 once it has learned anything (clean it up first) or if the new name is taken. Same endpoint patches options/sharing/schedule.

item.name: Gated site: is the browser session working?
item.description: Fetches the connector's start URL through the saved browser session and reports content vs a sign-in page. A saved profile alone proves nothing — this is what distinguishes 'signed in' from 'silently ingesting zero documents'.

item.name: Gated site: open a sign-in window
item.description: Opens a real Chromium window ON THE QUICKJOINER HOST for a web_scrape connector with use_browser=true. Background job — poll the session request above. 409 when one is already open or the host has no display (use `qj browser login <url>` there instead). The URL comes from the connector's own start_urls, never the request body.

item.name: Poll sync jobs (re-send until done)
item.description: Re-send until the job for your connector reads done/error/stopped. Shows current stage + percent while running. In the Collection Runner add an iteration delay, or use the logs SSE stream instead.

exec: pm.test('has a job for the connector', () => !!job);

item.name: Stream live logs (SSE)
item.description: Server-Sent Events. Postman renders the raw stream — read `data:` lines until `done`.

item.name: Upload a document (Word/PPT/Excel/PDF/…)
item.description: multipart/form-data — pick one or more files under the `files` key. Each is extracted and ingested into the rolling Uploads connector. Do not set Content-Type by hand; Postman adds the multipart boundary.

item.name: Ingest a server file path (JSON)
item.description: The /qj-friendly variant: ingest a file the server can read (copied into the uploads folder). Set `uploadPath` to an absolute path on the server host.

item.name: Ask a grounded question (SSE)
item.description:
Streams SSE events: thinking / delta / tool_call / tool_result / sources / candidates / answer / done. `project` and `session_id` are optional; if a session id comes back on the stream, capture it for the next call.

`tool_call` and `tool_result` carry JSON in `data` — {id, name, args} and {id, name, ok, summary, chars} — paired by `id` and interleaved with `thinking` in the real order the run happened, so a client can render it as a step-by-step trace. `summary` is a bounded preview; `chars` is the true size of the output the model received.

`sources` carries [{label, uri, link?, kind?, score?, snippet}] — the citable refs a tool result newly introduced, additive across the turn. It is what lets a citation of a readable title resolve to the page it came from and render as a link. `uri` is IDENTITY and is not always browsable (a cloned repo file is `<clone-url>::<path>`); `link` is where the citation should open, and is absent when there is no web address — link on `link`, never on `uri`.

item.name: Teach a fact
item.description: `share` (default false) decides who can read and cite the note. False keeps it private to the signed-in teacher (its own `notes:<user>` source); true teaches the commons, readable and citable by every user of the workspace. In open mode there is no signed-in user to own a note, so everything stays commons regardless.

item.name: Attach a file to a question (context, not memory)
item.description: multipart/form-data — pick file(s) under `files`. Returns attachment ids to pass as `attachment_ids` on the chat request. These are per-question context (extracted to text, injected into the turn), NOT ingested into memory, and auto-deleted after the retention window. Capture an id into `attachmentId` to try the download below.

item.name: Download a chat attachment (410 once expired)
item.description: Streams the original attached file. Returns 410 Gone once the retention sweep has deleted it (the chat history still shows the name + deletion date).

item.name: Learn an attachment into memory
item.description: Promote a per-question chat attachment into PERMANENT memory: the already-uploaded file is ingested into the rolling Uploads connector (chunked, embedded, graphed, citable). Attaching is context for one question by design; this is the explicit opt-in that makes it memory — the "Learning permanently" toggle in the UI. 410 once the retention sweep has deleted the bytes, 404 for an unknown id. `progress_token` is optional (client-minted) — pass one to make this request's real chunk-embedding progress readable via the next request while it's still running; omit it for the plain behaviour the CLI/agent's qj_api tool use.

item.name: Poll ingest progress
item.description: Real chunk-embedding progress for an in-flight ad-hoc ingest — poll this in parallel with a "Learn an attachment into memory" request sent with the same progress_token. Embedding a large document (e.g. a whole zip's concatenated text) can take minutes on a CPU-only machine; this is what a UI polls instead of showing nothing. 204 (empty body) if the token is unknown: never started, already finished and aged out (5 minutes), or nobody will ever start it — not an error. 200 body: {"done": <chunks embedded>, "total": <chunks total>}; total of 0 means extraction/chunking hasn't finished yet.

item.name: Unmined relationships (queue)
item.description: Documents that were ingested but whose relationship extraction never resolved. A connector that pulls a moving window (recent sprints) never re-provides them, so no sync retries it.

item.name: Mine unmined relationships
item.description: Starts a background job (source `graph relationships`) that re-reads the text already indexed for those documents and finishes their graph — no connector round-trip. Watch it via `GET /api/sync/graph relationships/logs`. 409 while another job runs or when graph.extract_triples is off. Add `?source_id=files:handbook` to scope it.

item.name: Preview a graph rebuild
item.description: Sizing + honesty read for the rebuild below. Returns `{documents, missing_payload, extraction_enabled}`. `missing_payload` counts documents ingested before their connector's structural claims (ADO dev-links/hierarchy, GitLab MR joins, Jira issue links, Octopus deployments) were persisted — a rebuild can add to and correct those but cannot authoritatively replace them, so their existing edges are preserved. Sync a source once to make its documents fully rebuildable. Add `?source_id=...` to scope it.

item.name: Rebuild the knowledge graph
item.description: Rebuilds the graph from documents ALREADY ingested — no connector round-trip, no re-chunk, no re-embed. For when the graph extractors changed but the documents did not. Starts a background job (source `knowledge graph`); watch it via `GET /api/sync/knowledge graph/logs`. 409 while another job runs. `with_triples=false` (default) is the deterministic rebuild and needs no LLM; `with_triples=true` also re-queues relationship mining — one model call per document, hours on a large corpus — and 409s when graph.extract_triples is off. Add `?source_id=...` to scope it.

item.name: 6 · OneDrive / SharePoint (per-user, on demand)
item.description:
This connector authenticates as a **person**, not with a static secret, and it never crawls: it ingests exactly the documents you point it at.

1. Create it with your Azure app registration's Application (client) ID — it saves even though it is not signed in yet, because the token is keyed to the connector.
2. Sign in: `Start sign-in` returns an `authorize_url`; open it in a browser and complete Microsoft sign-in (the redirect to `/api/oauth/callback` stores the token). In a terminal or container use `qj onedrive login <name>` (device code) instead — no redirect needed.
3. Learn specific documents by link or drive path. A folder learns the readable files under it.

Set `onedriveConnector`, `onedriveClientId` and `onedriveTarget` in the collection variables.

item.name: Create OneDrive connector
item.description: `access` requests only the delegated Graph scopes you need: my_drive → Files.Read, shared_with_me → Files.Read.All, sharepoint → Sites.Read.All (usually admin consent). The response's `test.message` says "not signed in yet" — expected.

item.name: Start sign-in (authorization code + PKCE)
item.description: Returns `authorize_url`. Open it in a browser; the redirect to `/api/oauth/callback` stores the token server-side. `qj onedrive login <name>` is the no-browser alternative.

item.name: Sign-in status
item.description: Who the connector acts as and how many documents it has learned. Never returns the tokens.

item.name: Learn documents on demand
item.description: Resolves each target with the signed-in user's own access, extracts text and ingests it. `notes` lists everything NOT learned and why (unsupported type, too large, or an image — images need vision support, which is on the roadmap). `warning` restates that learned documents join the workspace's shared memory.

item.name: Sign out
item.description: Deletes the stored Microsoft 365 refresh token. Deleting the connector does this automatically — a live refresh token must not outlive its connector.

item.name: 7 · Documents, labels & scoped questions
item.description:
See what a connector ingested, label it, and ask a question limited to that slice.

`uri_prefix` picks the label granularity: '' = whole connector, a folder path = that folder AND files ingested into it later, a full document uri = one document. A scope on `POST /api/chat` is resolved server-side into a real pre-filter on both retrieval legs, and live tools for connectors outside the scope are withheld for that turn.

item.name: List a source's documents
item.description: Each document with the labels that apply to it, including ones inherited from its folder or the connector — resolved at read time, so folder tags cover later files. Each document also carries `metadata` — a small connector-supplied JSON blob for UI display only, `{}` for every connector that doesn't set it. Azure DevOps stamps work_item_type/state/team/sprint/parent_id/changed_date/closed_date there, which is what the document browser uses to render TFS work items as an Epic/Feature/Story/Task tree.

item.name: List an archive's contents
item.description: A .zip ingests as ONE document (its members' text concatenated — see ingest/extract._extract_zip), so the listing above shows it as one opaque row. This recovers the member list — and any files it skipped, and why — from the document's own extracted text (there's no separate column for it). `doc_id` is one of the doc_id values from the request above. Returns {"members": [...], "notes": [...]} — empty lists (not an error) for a document that isn't an archive.

item.name: Tag a folder
item.description: Files ingested into this folder later inherit the tag automatically. Use uri_prefix '' for the whole connector, or a full document uri for just one document.

item.name: List all labels
item.description: Every tag/aka in the workspace — what the UI's question-scope picker offers.

item.name: Ask a scoped question
item.description: SSE, like the unscoped ask. Searches strictly less rather than filtering afterwards. A scoped 'no results' is reported as 'not in the sources you scoped to', never as 'never learned' — the model is told it only searched a slice.

item.name: Remove a label
item.description: Removing a folder/connector label removes it from every document it covered.

item.name: Reset ALL memory (keep connectors)
item.description: DANGER — wipes every ingested document, vector and graph edge across the whole workspace. Runs as a background job (returns {job}, source 'all memory') — watch it via the sync logs stream (source `all memory`) or the activity feed. Refuses (409) while any sync runs.

item.name: 9 · Skills (packaged expertise)
item.description:
A skill is a folder holding SKILL.md (YAML frontmatter + markdown), optionally with references/ and scripts/ — the open Agent Skills format Claude Code and GitHub Copilot both read, so a skill written for either works here unmodified.

Two tiers, because they are different acts: USING one is open to everybody, and so is supplying YOUR OWN credentials for it; INSTALLING / removing / re-scoping one is admin only, because a skill may bundle scripts and a script runs with the server's privileges.

A skill whose scripts read credentials is registered user-scoped on arrival: it will not run until the calling person supplies those values, and never falls back to whatever the server holds under the same names. So the list request answers 'is this ready FOR ME', not 'does this exist'. Secrets are encrypted at rest and write-only — no endpoint anywhere reads a value back out.

item.name: List skills (per-caller readiness)
item.description: Every discovered skill with its scope, what it requires, and — for THIS caller — whether it is ready (`ready`, `missing`). A scoped skill with missing credentials is still listed rather than hidden, so a client can say exactly what to set. `detected_env` is what its scripts look like they read: a suggestion for the admin form, never the gate. `required_env` is the gate.

item.name: Install a skill (.zip, admin)
item.description:
multipart/form-data — pick a .zip containing SKILL.md under the `file` key (see the skillZip variable). Postman adds the multipart boundary; do not set Content-Type by hand.

Replacement is total: a re-upload removes the previous folder first, so a script the new version no longer mentions cannot survive to be run. The stored configuration for that name is NOT reset — an admin's scope decision outlives the files. 400 with a stated reason for an unreadable archive, no SKILL.md, or a size/member overrun; 403 for a non-admin.

item.name: Configure a skill (admin)
item.description:
Override what the skill's own frontmatter declares; every field is optional. `scope` is `open` (anyone may run it, no credentials) or `user` (it runs with each person's own values).

This is the correction path for detection over-reaching: a real skill's scripts read tuning flags alongside credentials and only a human can tell them apart, so trim `required_env` to what genuinely gates it. The stored row is authoritative from here on — rediscovery never overwrites it.

item.name: List my secret names (never values)
item.description: Which names this caller has set (`mine`) and which are set workspace-wide (`workspace`). Presence, never content — no endpoint anywhere reads a stored value back out. A personal value overrides the workspace one of the same name.

item.name: Set one of my secrets
item.description: Store one credential, encrypted at rest. `scope: user` (the default) is yours alone and overrides a workspace value of the same name — every signed-in user may do this, since it is their own credential and reaches nobody else's. `scope: workspace` is an admin's shared default (an endpoint URL, a tenant id) that everyone inherits, and needs the admin tier.

item.name: Remove one of my secrets
item.description: `scope=user` (default) removes yours; `scope=workspace` removes the shared one and needs the admin tier.

item.name: Remove a skill (admin)
item.description: Deletes the skill's folder from the workspace and forgets its configuration. Requires the skills:delete capability, which is in the DANGER tier — reaching this from chat additionally needs a typed confirm=true. 409 for a skill discovered under a personal ~/.claude/skills or ~/.copilot/skills — that belongs to the operator's own tooling, not to QuickJoiner; disable it instead (PATCH {"enabled": false}, or qj skills disable). Returns {removed, configuration_forgotten}. Stored secrets are NOT removed — a value may serve other skills; clear one via DELETE /api/skills/secrets/{key}.

item.name: 10 · Promotion (personal → organisation)
item.description:
A taught note is private to its author by default (knowledge scopes). That is right, and on its own a dead end: the useful half of what a joiner works out is exactly what the next joiner needs. This is the path across, and it is a REVIEW rather than a button, because one person's unreviewed assertion must not become citable org truth by accident.

Three steps, three capabilities: OFFER (promotions:request, every user — your own documents only, and it publishes nothing); REVIEW (promotions:review, editor and admin — the queue, plus the one narrow read exception in the whole knowledge-scopes model: a reviewer may open a document that is still private, but only while its author has it offered); DECIDE.

Approval is a METADATA FLIP, NOT A COPY: the document moves to the ownerless `promoted:org` bucket keeping the same doc_id, chunks, vectors, citations and graph edges. Nothing is re-uploaded, re-chunked or re-embedded.

Set {{promoteDocId}} first.

item.name: Offer one of your documents to the organisation
item.description:
Queue one of YOUR OWN private documents for review. `note` is why the org should have it. This changes nothing about who can read it — it stays private to you until a reviewer approves.

400 if the document is already readable by everyone (a promotion that would be a no-op is refused rather than reported as success), if it is not yours, or if it is already queued.

item.name: The review queue (editor/admin)
item.description: Everything people have offered, oldest first — a backlog, not a feed. This is `promotions:review`, NOT an ordinary read capability: every row is a document still private to its author, listed only because they offered it. A viewer gets 403.

item.name: Read an offered document (reviewer)
item.description: The document's actual text, so a reviewer decides on what it says rather than on its title. The one deliberate exception to knowledge scopes, kept narrow: scoped to documents in `requested` state and to this endpoint alone, with retrieval untouched. 404 for anything not currently awaiting review — exactly as if it did not exist.

item.name: Approve or decline (reviewer)
item.description:
`approve: true` re-homes the document to the shared `promoted:org` bucket — an ownerless commons source, which is what makes every visibility predicate already in the codebase start including it with no read-path change at all. `approve: false` leaves it exactly where it was and records `note` as a reason the author can act on.

Verify with the search request in folder 4 as a DIFFERENT user: empty before, a hit after.
